candidate.blueprint_topic: Management of Care — appropriate collaboration with a nonclinical birth-support professional
candidate.educational_objective: Collaborate with a doula as a nonclinical support professional who complements nursing and obstetric care by providing physical, emotional, educational, and communication support without assuming clinical assessment, treatment, or medication-administration functions.

options.A: Invite the doula to provide comfort measures, emotional support, and help the client communicate preferences while the RN continues clinical nursing care.
options.B: Ask the doula to independently interpret changes in the fetal heart rate tracing and recommend whether obstetric intervention is needed.
options.C: Delegate administration of a prescribed as-needed analgesic to the doula when the RN is caring for another client.
options.D: Require the doula to stop bedside labor support once the RN is present so that only one person provides continuous emotional support.

candidate.rationale: A is correct. Current ACOG guidance describes the doula's role as complementary to the medical team and identifies physical and emotional support, education, support for self-advocacy, communication of preferences, and labor comfort measures as appropriate doula functions. CMS likewise describes doula services as emotional, physical, and informational support provided by a nonclinical trained professional. B is incorrect because independent fetal-monitor interpretation and recommendations for obstetric intervention are clinical functions, not nonclinical doula support. C is incorrect because medication administration is a clinical task and is outside the nonclinical doula role. D is incorrect because doula support is intended to complement clinical care; ACOG specifically recommends respectful clinician-doula teamwork rather than excluding the doula when clinical staff are present.
candidate.source_claim_supported: Doulas are nonclinical support professionals whose role complements the clinical team through physical, emotional, educational, informational, advocacy, and communication support rather than clinical assessment or treatment.
candidate.source_document_title: Partnering With Doulas in Clinical Settings, Committee Statement No. 31; Transforming Maternal Health (TMaH) Model Frequently Asked Questions
candidate.source_locator: ACOG Committee Statement No. 31 — Background: doula work is complementary to the medical team; doulas support self-advocacy, provide physical and emotional support, help clients navigate medical decisions and communicate preferences, and provide education. Recommendations and Conclusions: create respectful teams that include doulas; continuous support includes comfort measures and reassurance. CMS TMaH Model FAQ, Question 20 'What doula care services will be covered in the TMaH Model?': doula services are emotional, physical, and informational support provided by a nonclinical trained professional during pregnancy, delivery, and after childbirth.
candidate.source_organization: American College of Obstetricians & Gynecologists (ACOG); Centers for Medicare & Medicaid Services (CMS)
candidate.source_version_date: ACOG Committee Statement No. 31, August 2026, published online July 16, 2026; CMS TMaH FAQ current page accessed 2026-08-17
candidate.stem: A laboring client has a doula in addition to the RN and obstetric clinician. Which action by the RN best reflects appropriate collaboration with the doula?
